input.name: Plot Geometry / Shape
input.description: Geometric morphology of the boundary perimeter as surveyed on site.

input.name: Length to Width Ratio (Proportion)
input.description: Proportion of plot length to width (Length / Width). Ideal is 1:1 (Square) or 1:1.25 to 1:1.5 (Auspicious Rectangle). Ratios beyond 1:2.0 represent Dirgha-shala / excessive elongation.

input.name: Natural Slope / Terrain Gradient
input.description: Dominant natural downward slope of the terrain surface.

input.name: Broad Geological Contour (Bhūmi-Pṛṣṭha)
input.description: Macro-topography of the terrain according to classical taxonomy: Gajapṛṣṭha (high in S/W/SW, low in N/E/NE), Kūrmapṛṣṭha (high center, low periphery), Daityapṛṣṭha (high in N/E/NE, low in S/W/SW), Nāgapṛṣṭha (undulating E-W ridges).

input.name: Soil Color (Excavated Strata)
input.description: Color of virgin subsoil at 1 cubit depth. Classically associated with Guṇa and suitability.

input.name: Soil Odor / Smell
input.description: Olfactory test of moist virgin soil. Foul odors indicate decomposing organic matter, shallow water table, or toxic chemical strata.

input.name: Compaction Pit Test (Garta-Pūraṇa)
input.description: A 1-cubit (approx. 18-24 inches) cubic pit is dug and the excavated soil is poured back without manual tamping. Surplus earth indicates dense preconsolidated soil (high bearing capacity); sunken deficit indicates loose, porous, collapsable soil.

input.name: Water Percolation & Retention Test (Jala-Parīkṣā)
input.description: The excavated pit is filled with water at sunset and inspected at dawn. Substantial retained water demonstrates cohesive impermeable strata; bone-dry cracked ground indicates excessive void ratio, fissures, or subterranean cavities.

input.name: Primary Road Facing / Frontage
input.description: Direction from which primary access road fronts the property.

input.name: Street Focus / T-Junction Thrust (Vīthi-Śūla)
input.description: Presence and orientation of an oncoming road terminating directly perpendicular to the plot boundary.

input.name: Deviation Angle from Geographic North (Śaṅku Dig-Nirṇaya)
input.description: Angular tilt of the plot's primary axis relative to true magnetic/geographic North. Plots with 0-5° are Cardinal (Sama-dig); >15° are Vidiśa (Diagonal).

input.name: Corner Extensions & Cuts (Koṇa-Vṛddhi / Kartana)
input.description: Structural deviation from 90° orthogonality at the plot corners.

rule.element_mahabhuta: Prithvi & Akasha (Equilibrium of all five Mahābhūtas)
rule.classical_source: Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 12; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 14; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 85
rule.classical_sloka: caturaśrā sarveṣāṃ vāstūnāṃ śubhadā sadā | sarva-kāma-phalā nṝṇāṃ dhana-dhānya-vivardhinī ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: A square plot has four equal sides and four 90° right angles. It establishes complete energetic symmetry and balance of the cardinal poles, granting holistic health, mental clarity, and enduring wealth.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Perfect geometric symmetry eliminates torsional moments during seismic events, ensures equal daylight distribution, and optimizes structural load paths.
rule.classical_remedy: None required. Consecrate the central Brahmasthāna as an open-to-sky courtyard or lightweight zone.

rule.classical_source: Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 13; Mānasāra Ch. 3 v. 22; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 16
rule.classical_sloka: āyatā śubhadā nityaṃ catur-varga-phala-pradā | dīrghatve dvy-ardha-mātraṃ tu śastam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: An oblong rectangular plot with length-to-width ratio between 1:1.25 and 1:1.50, aligned North-South or East-West, is highly auspicious, bestowing success in worldly affairs and long life.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Optimal aspect ratio facilitates natural cross-ventilation, clear spatial zoning between public and private domains, and efficient plumbing distribution.
rule.classical_remedy: Ensure the ratio does not exceed 1:2. If ratio is greater than 2:1, divide the plot physically or energetically using compound walls or hedging.

rule.direction_zone: Front facing East or North; Broad in Rear (West/South)
rule.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 34; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 24
rule.classical_sloka: gomukhaṃ tu sadā śastaṃ gṛheṣu dhanavardhanam | paścādvistīrṇamagre tu saṅkṣiptaṃ gomukhaṃ smṛtam ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Narrow in the front (road side) and broad in the back. When the narrow front faces East or North and the broad back rests in South or West, it forms the sacred Gomukhi configuration, accumulating and preserving family wealth and harmony.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Funnel geometry acts as an acoustic and aerodynamic buffer against front street dust and noise while maximizing quiet, private open space in the rear.
rule.classical_remedy: If the front faces South or West, it reverses the polarity; correct by planting dense bamboo/ficus hedges in the front and keeping the rear open.

rule.direction_zone: Front facing North/East; Narrow in Rear
rule.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 35; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 16
rule.classical_sloka: vyāghra-vaktre tu vāṇijyaṃ rāja-saṃsevane hitam | vāsārthaṃ naiva kartavyaṃ putradāra-vināśanam ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Broad at the front and narrow at the rear. Auspicious for commercial ventures, corporate headquarters, public retail, or administrative buildings, but prohibited for domestic residences as it disperses domestic tranquility.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Wide street frontage provides excellent visual exposure, branding frontage, and ingress capacity for commercial foot traffic, but compromises residential privacy.
rule.classical_remedy: For residential use on a Shermukhi plot, construct a straight boundary wall to partition off the irregular triangular side wedges, rendering the habitable plot a true rectangle.

rule.classical_source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 87; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 28; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 17
rule.classical_sloka: trikoṇe vahnibhītiḥ syād rāja-daṇḍas tathaiva ca | kulanāśo bhavet tatra na kuryāt tatra mandiram ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Triangular plots generate aggressive angular convergence (Agni-koṇa dynamics), predisposing occupants to constant litigation, fire accidents, internal bickering, and royal/governmental penalties.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Acute corner angles (<60°) produce severe internal stress concentrations, dead unusable corners with stagnant air, and complicated structural roof framing.
rule.classical_remedy: Erect internal perimeter walls or heavy evergreen hedges to carve out an internal square or rectangle, relegating the triangular acute corners to external landscaped gardens with a dedicated Agni yantra.

rule.classical_source: Mānasāra Ch. 3 v. 30; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 18; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 14
rule.classical_sloka: vṛttā tu yā mahī loke sā śastā suraveśmani | narāṇāṃ na hitā sā hi dāridrya-maraṇāvahā ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Circular plots lack stabilizing cardinal corners. Classical treatises permit circular plots solely for circular temples, Buddhist stupas, civic amphitheaters, or ascetic hermitages; residential use causes poverty and lack of foundation.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Curvilinear boundaries make standard orthogonal construction uneconomical and generate unstable acoustic reflections focusing sound towards the center.
rule.classical_remedy: Square off the living compound inside the circle by creating four corner landscape gardens.

rule.classical_source: Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 32; Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 38
rule.classical_sloka: viṣama-bāhuṣu nityaṃ śatrubhītiḥ prajāyate | dravyasaṅkṣayaḥ kalahaḥ syād vāstudoṣeṇa sarvadā ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Plots with unequal non-parallel sides and asymmetric corner angles cause chaotic energy distribution, leading to perpetual enemy fear, unexpected financial drain, and discord among partners.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Irregular boundaries generate asymmetric seismic torsional shears and complicate structural alignment.
rule.classical_remedy: Survey the plot, establish an orthogonal rectangle inside, and surrender the residual irregular margins to outer compound greenery or parking.

rule.classical_source: Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 20; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 26
rule.classical_sloka: śakaṭākṛti-yā bhūmiḥ sā sarvārtha-vināśinī | nṛṇāṃ dāridryadā nityaṃ pravāsa-maraṇa-pradā ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Shaped like a bullock cart (narrow in middle, wide at front and back), it forces continuous wandering, severe financial penury, and premature loss of family heads.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Constricted central waist restricts airflow, utilities, and emergency egress routes between front and back zones.
rule.classical_remedy: Straighten the waist with compound boundary adjustments or partition into two separate self-contained rectangular units.

rule.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 30; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 5; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 88
rule.classical_sloka: īśāna-plavanā bhūmiḥ sarvasiddhividhāyinī | āyur-ārogya-sampattir vijayo vṛddhir uttamā ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: A plot sloping down towards the North-East (Īśāna-plava) is the supreme topographical contour. It allows uninterrupted absorption of early morning ultraviolet-enriched solar radiation and magnetic flux, bestowing health, intellect, and spiritual and material abundance.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Natural surface runoff discharges towards the NE corner, allowing clean stormwater gravity disposal without contaminating southern living zones.
rule.classical_remedy: None needed. Keep this lowest quadrant clean, open, and free of massive masonry loads.

rule.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 30; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 45
rule.classical_sloka: pūrva-plavā vṛddhikarī sarva-sampat-pradāyinī | sūrya-tejo-samāyuktā kuloddhāra-karī sadā ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: An Eastward slope (Pūrva-plava / Indra-vīthi) welcomes the rising sun across the site, promoting physical vitality, professional status, enlightenment, and harmonious governance.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Maximizes passive solar heat gain in winter mornings while enabling rapid drying of nocturnal dampness.
rule.classical_remedy: Maintain low boundary wall on East and higher boundary wall on West.

rule.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 30; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 6
rule.classical_sloka: dhanadā cottarā plavā vidyā-dhana-samṛddhidā | kauberasya prasādena kīrti-sampad-vivardhinī ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: A Northward slope (Uttara-plava / Soma-vīthi) draws the Earth's geomagnetic lines of force freely across the plot, conferring wealth, career advancements, intellectual sharpness, and commercial success.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Shielded from harsh southern glare while receiving continuous diffused ambient northern light (ideal for studies and studios).
rule.classical_remedy: Keep Northern perimeter open with light permeable railings.

rule.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 31; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 49; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 8
rule.classical_sloka: nairṛtyāṃ ca duryogaḥ kulanāśaḥ prajāyate | dāridryaṃ vyādhi-saṃpāto mṛtyur vā maraṇāntikam ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: A downward slope towards the South-West (Nairṛtya-plava / Daityapṛṣṭha) is a catastrophic defect. It exposes the vulnerable southwest to drainage erosion while depressing the earth element, resulting in chronic health crises, bankruptcy, addiction, and premature demise of the head of the house.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Causes heavy stormwater to pool in the SW, weakening foundation soils under maximum afternoon thermal expansion and leading to differential settlement.
rule.classical_remedy: Extensive civil engineering earthwork: fill the SW quadrant with compacted gravel/earth to make it the highest elevation; construct heavy retaining walls and terrace slopes toward the North-East.

rule.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 31; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 89
rule.classical_sloka: dakṣiṇa-plavā mṛtyukārī vartanāśī vināśinī | vyādhi-śokākulā nityaṃ nārīṇāṃ ca vināśanī ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Sloping down to the South drains vital life force into the realm of Yama, causing chronic illnesses, blood disorders, legal persecution, and premature decline of female family members.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Southern drainage often leads to thermal overheating and excessive desiccation of exposed soil slopes during summer months.
rule.classical_remedy: Build a high, massive southern compound wall; install heavy landscaping boulders in the South to artificially elevate and anchor the terrain.

rule.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 31; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 7
rule.classical_sloka: vartanāśī ca paścimā putrahāni-karī smṛtā | dravyasaṅkṣaya-kāriṇī pravāsa-jananī sadā ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: A Westward slope causes ongoing financial drain, delayed achievements, and children abandoning home.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Direct exposure of downward slopes to blazing western afternoon infrared radiation creates severe microclimate heat buildup.
rule.classical_remedy: Elevate western plinth with retaining walls and plant tall shade trees (e.g. Ashoka, Neem) along the western boundary.

rule.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 31; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 90
rule.classical_sloka: āgneyyāṃ dāha-santāpo rājadveṣas tathaiva ca | putra-mitra-kalatraiś ca virodho jāyate mahān ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Sloping down to the South-East fuels unrestrained fire energy, leading to accidental fires, electrical breakdowns, anger issues, and high medical expenses.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Creates an undesirable drainage runoff trap adjacent to kitchen/utility zones.
rule.classical_remedy: Backfill SE to make it higher than the NE/North; install a copper swastika or copper rod grid in the SE corner.

rule.classical_source: Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 31; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 51
rule.classical_sloka: vāyavyāṃ roga-uccāṭam aśāntir dhana-saṅkṣayaḥ | cañcalā sampado nityaṃ bāndhava-dveṣa eva ca ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Sloping down to the North-West causes wind-element instability, mental restlessness, insomnia, strained neighborly ties, and chronic respiratory or nervous conditions.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Funneling of chilly prevailing northwest winter winds into a depression causes dampness and energy loss.
rule.classical_remedy: Level the NW; plant wind-breaking trees and install brass/silver energy harmonizers.

rule.classical_source: Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 40; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 10
rule.classical_sloka: kūrmapṛṣṭhā samākhyātā madhye tūnnatasaṃsthitā | sarva-sampat-karī nṝṇāṃ sthirāyur-dhana-vardhinī ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Center elevated with gentle slopes outward like a tortoise shell (Kūrmapṛṣṭha). Promotes longevity, emotional stability, and robust financial accumulation.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Prevents stormwater from ponding near the building foundation, draining natural runoff outward to municipal perimeters.
rule.classical_remedy: Channel the perimeter drainage so that it collects and exits predominantly through the North-East.

rule.classical_source: Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 42; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 92
rule.classical_sloka: madhye nimnā mahī yā syād gartā sarvavināśinī | tasyāṃ vāso na kartavyo dāridrya-kalanāvahaḥ ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Center sunken with perimeter elevated creates a basin or crater (Raurava / Garta). It collapses the Brahmasthāna, inflicting crushing poverty, mental depression, and total family ruin.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Water ponds directly beneath or around the core building, saturating foundations and generating rising damp and mold.
rule.classical_remedy: Must be mechanically backfilled with clean compacted red or river soil until the center is level or slightly higher than the perimeter.

rule.classical_source: Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 38; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 9
rule.classical_sloka: dakṣiṇa-paścimonnata-bhūmir gajapṛṣṭheti kīrtitā | āyur-dhana-kulodbhūtā sarvasaukhyakarī nṛṇām ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Elevated in the South, South-West, and West; descending gently toward North, East, and North-East. Emulates an elephant's back (Gajapṛṣṭha), granting immense strength, social honor, long lifespan, and enduring prosperity.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Shields the dwelling from southwest storms and afternoon solar glare while admitting morning sun and northern breezes.
rule.classical_remedy: Maintain this natural contour without excavating the southern or western shoulders.

rule.classical_source: Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 41; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 11
rule.classical_sloka: īśāna-pūrva-saṃsthitir unnatā daityapṛṣṭhakā | dravyāyuḥ-suta-nāśāya nityaṃ roga-bhayāvahā ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Elevated in the North-East and North; plunging down toward the South and South-West. Designated Daityapṛṣṭha (Demon back), it reverses cosmic polarity, annihilating wealth, lifespan, and progeny.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Blocks morning sunlight and geomagnetic flux while channeling all runoff into the high-heat SW corner.
rule.classical_remedy: Extensive civil earth re-engineering: cut down the NE ridge and use it to fill the SW depression.

rule.classical_source: Mānasāra Ch. 3 v. 15-18; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 15
rule.classical_sloka: aratni-mātre khāte tu pūrite tair mṛdādibhiḥ | adhike dravyam uddiṣṭaṃ same madhyamadhīmatā | hīne dāridryam ākhyātaṃ tasmāt hīnaṃ vivarjayet ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Digging a 1-cubit pit and refilling it with the dug earth leaves surplus soil overflowing. Indicates densely preconsolidated soil with low void ratio and high safe bearing capacity; guarantees domestic durability and wealth.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: High relative compaction, low void ratio ($e < 0.5$), minimal risk of settlement under structural foundations.
rule.classical_remedy: None required. Standard shallow isolated footing is sufficient.

rule.classical_source: Mānasāra Ch. 3 v. 18; Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 16
rule.classical_sloka: hīne dāridryam āpnoti kṣayaṃ vā samupāgatam |
rule.plain_language_explanation: Excavated earth fails to fill back the pit, sinking into a depression. Indicates porous, highly compressible, loose soil liable to differential structural settlement; causes financial ruin.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: High void ratio ($e > 1.0$), collapsable or organic soil matrix; acute danger of foundation cracking.
rule.classical_remedy: Excavate down to hard bedrock or dense stratum; replace loose topsoil with compacted engineered sand/gravel; design raft foundation or under-reamed piles.

rule.classical_source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 16; Mānasāra Ch. 3 v. 20
rule.classical_sloka: jala-pūrṇa-karte dṛṣṭe prātar dravya-samṛddhidā |
rule.plain_language_explanation: Water poured into the test pit at sunset remains standing at dawn. Confirms cohesive, impermeable subsoil capable of holding foundation loads without rapid leaching.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Cohesive clayey-silt matrix preventing subterranean erosion or piping failures under water-table fluctuations.
rule.classical_remedy: Provide adequate peripheral subsoil plinth drainage to prevent surface dampness.

rule.classical_source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 17; Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 25
rule.classical_sloka: kṣīṇe toye vināśaḥ syāt paribhramaṇa-kārakam |
rule.plain_language_explanation: Water in the test pit drains away completely, leaving cracked dry mud. Reveals subterranean fissures, excessive macropores, or subterranean sinkholes; drives occupants into wandering and financial exhaustion.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: High hydraulic conductivity, loose gravel/karst cavities, high vulnerability to washouts.
rule.classical_remedy: Grout subterranean cavities with cement-bentonite slurry; install deep foundation piers down to non-porous strata.

rule.classical_source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 94; Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 50
rule.classical_sloka: īśāne vīthi-śūlaṃ tu sarva-sampatti-kārakam | vidyā-dhana-samṛddhiḥ syāt kīrti-vardhana-m-uttamam ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: An oncoming street focus hitting the plot from the North of North-East (Uchha Vīthi-śūla). Accelerates cosmic magnetic and water energy into the plot, fostering academic genius, financial growth, and family renown.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Provides an unobstructed light and air ventilation corridor from the cool, glare-free northern sector.
rule.classical_remedy: Keep entrance gate wide, install low landscaping, and ensure front driveway is clean and welcoming.

rule.classical_source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 94; Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 50
rule.classical_sloka: aīndre ca śubhadaṃ viddhi putrapautra-vivardhanam |
rule.plain_language_explanation: A street thrust hitting from the East of North-East. Channels unhindered morning solar radiation, conferring vitality, public prestige, and noble lineage.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Direct unimpeded solar penetration into the compound, sterilizing pathogenic dampness.
rule.classical_remedy: No remedy needed. Frame the entry with pleasant flowering plants or a water basin.

rule.classical_source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 95; Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 52
rule.classical_sloka: nairṛtye vīthi-śūle tu gṛhapater maraṇaṃ bhavet | vyādhayaḥ śatru-vṛddhiś ca dāridryaṃ caiva dāruṇam ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: An oncoming road thrusting directly into the South of South-West (Maha Vīthi-śūla). The kinetic vehicular and wind momentum pierces the vital anchor of the site, causing fatal accidents, severe physical handicaps, sudden bankruptcy, and death of the householder.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Direct line-of-sight for oncoming high-beam traffic glare, brake-failure vehicular impact risk, and continuous acoustic vibration assaulting the master bedroom.
rule.classical_remedy: Build a heavy reinforced concrete barrier wall; offset the entrance gate completely away from the thrust axis; install a large convex mirror, a defensive row of dense Ashoka/Ficus trees, and a consecrated lead yantra.

rule.classical_source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 53 v. 95; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 38 v. 30
rule.classical_sloka: paścima-nairṛte śūle strī-vināśo dhana-kṣayaḥ |
rule.plain_language_explanation: A street thrust hitting from the West of South-West. Inflicts acute depression, financial collapse, long-term lawsuits, and loss of life.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Extreme vulnerability to head-on collision from vehicles exiting highway/road tangents; dust storms and thermal wind blast.
rule.classical_remedy: Construct a curved offset compound wall, plant a buffer thicket of leaden-rooted trees, and place defensive quartz pyramids along the impact line.

rule.classical_source: Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 32; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 58; Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 55
rule.classical_sloka: īśānasya ca vṛddhau tu sarva-sampatti-vardhanam | putrapautra-samṛddhiḥ syāj jñāna-dharmābhivṛddhidā ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: An extension or projection in the North-East corner (Īśāna-vṛddhi) where the corner angle is acute (<90°), drawing extra perimeter into the NE. Magnifies divine grace, spiritual wisdom, academic eminence, and sustained financial abundance.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Maximizes the surface area capturing morning diffuse sunlight and geomagnetic flux while increasing open garden area.
rule.classical_remedy: None required. Maintain this extended space for light gardening, meditation gazebo, or water feature.

rule.classical_source: Mayamata Ch. 3 v. 33; Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra Ch. 8 v. 59; Viśvakarma Prakāśa Ch. 1 v. 56
rule.classical_sloka: īśāne khaṇḍite gehe santater nāśam ādiśet | dāridryaṃ caiva rogaś ca buddhi-bhranśo bhaved dhruvam ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: A missing or cut North-East corner (Īśāna-kartana). In Vedic anthropomorphism, this represents the severing of the head of the Vāstu Puruṣa; leads to neurological disorders, mental confusion, loss of progeny, and utter financial stagnation.
rule.engineering_physical_rationale: Deprives the building of morning sunlight and cross-ventilation breezes, creating gloomy interiors.
rule.classical_remedy: Energetically restore the missing corner by installing full-length mirrors on the truncated walls, embedding copper/zinc energy rods in the soil along the virtual rectangular boundary, or installing a consecrated Īśāna Yantra.

tools.interpretation: In classical Sthāpatya Veda, the plot (Bhūmi) is not an inert physical surface, but a living bio-energetic organism known as the Vāstu Puruṣa. Analysis of a plot synthesizes macroscopic topography (Bhūmi-Pṛṣṭha: Gajapṛṣṭha vs Daityapṛṣṭha), precise boundary geometry (Kṣetra-Saṃsthāna), geotechnical load-bearing capacity (Garta-pūraṇa and Jala-parīkṣā), solar geometry (Plava / natural slope towards North and East), and street kinetic vectors (Vīthi-śūla). The primary objective is to maximize the absorption of early morning solar ultraviolet-A rays and geomagnetic lines of force (Jaiva-ūrjā) descending from the North-East, while grounding and shielding the dwelling against the harsh infrared thermal and tectonic stresses of the South-West.
tools.variation_note: Classical regional treatises demonstrate deliberate geographical adaptations: 1. Northern & Rajasthani tradition (Viśvakarma Prakāśa, Aparājitapṛcchā) emphasizes high protective boundary walls, deep square compounds, and defense against abrasive desert sandstorms and severe southern heat. 2. Southern Drāviḍa tradition (Mānasāra, Mayamata) focuses on exact mathematical orientation via gnomonic shadow circles (Śaṅku-dig-nirṇaya) and proportional modularity using the Āyādi-ṣaḍvarga formulas. 3. Kerala tradition (Manuṣyālaya Candrikā) is adapted to torrential tropical rainfall; it mandates that natural drainage must slope North-East, enforces uncompromised central open-air courtyards (Nālukettu), and relaxes certain rigid soil color constraints due to ubiquitous laterite soil.

rule.scientific_environmental_rationale: High moisture immediately adjacent to electrical wiring and thermal kitchen appliances increases short-circuit hazards and dampness.
rule.classical_remedy: Decommission the sump or borewell if feasible; fill with dry sand and seal with a consecrated copper plate. rule.classical_remedy: Mandatory closure: drill a replacement borewell in the North-East, then thoroughly backfill the SW well with layers of river gravel, yellow clay, and energized lead rods. rule.classical_remedy: Surround the well rim with heavy red sandstone slabs, place lead-embedded pyramids, and cultivate dense Tulasi or Ashoka trees to absorb excess moisture.

rule.plain_language_explanation: Underground water in the North-West destabilizes mental equilibrium, bringing nervous strain, enemy hostility, unmanageable debts, and continuous travel.
rule.scientific_environmental_rationale: Chilly winter winds over cold underground water exacerbate domestic dampness and airborne mold spores.
rule.classical_remedy: Construct a raised white marble border around the opening, bind with a silver strip, and restrict water usage to irrigation/cleaning.

rule.classical_remedy: Must be permanently sealed. Pump out standing water, fill completely with compacted clean gravel, sand, and sacred clay, and seal with a consecrated granite or marble slab.

rule.plain_language_explanation: Varāhamihira's Dakārgala bio-indicators for locating underground aquifers: 1. Arjuna or Jambu tree with a termite mound (Valmīka) to its North indicates sweet water at shallow depth (3-5 Puruṣas / 18-30 ft) to the East or West. 2. Vetasa (reed cane) thriving in dry land confirms an active subterranean vein directly underneath.
rule.scientific_environmental_rationale: Phreatophytic tree roots (Arjuna, Jamun) penetrate deeply into subsoil aquifers; subterranean termite colonies require constant high relative humidity (90%+) and construct mounds directly above moisture veins.
rule.classical_remedy: Utilize these natural bio-indicators to site domestic wells rather than drilling blindly.

rule.classical_source: Bṛhat Saṃhitā Ch. 54 v. 121-122
rule.classical_sloka: añjana-mustā-uśīraiḥ sa-lodhra-katakaiḥ kṛtaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ | yoge'nena payāṃsi bhavanti vimalāni sugandhīni ||
rule.plain_language_explanation: Classical water clarification and purification formula: Combine powdered Kataka seeds (Strychnos potatorum / clearing nut), Mustā root (Cyperus rotundus), Uśīra root (Vetiveria zizanioides / vetiver), Lodhra bark, and Añjana. Added to turbid, brackish, or foul-smelling well water, it clears suspended matter, neutralizes odor, and makes the water sparkling clear, sweet, and safe.
rule.scientific_environmental_rationale: Kataka seed proteins act as natural polyelectrolyte coagulants that bind colloidal clay particles within minutes (matching modern alum coagulants); Vetiver and Mustā possess powerful antimicrobial essential oils that adsorb volatile sulfides and inhibit bacterial growth.
rule.classical_remedy: Treat stagnant tanks or wells periodically with Kataka and Vetiver root sachets to maintain biological freshness naturally.

tools.interpretation: In the classical canon of Vedic architecture, water (Jala-tattva) is treated as the primary carrier of prāṇic vitality and financial liquidity. The science of Jala-Vinyāsa operates under a rigorous dual-polarity principle balancing mass and elemental qualities: 1. Subterranean excavations (wells, sumps, borewells) create cavities of low gravitational density, which harmonize with the light, receptive, divine sectors of the North-East, North, and East, but create catastrophic vacuums if dug into the heavy foundational Earth zone of the South-West or the central navel (Brahmasthāna). 2. Conversely, overhead water tanks represent massive static loads (structural deadweight), which harmonize with the South-West and West where ballast is required to anchor the structure, but crush mental and spiritual well-being if placed atop the North-East. 3. Biological sewage (septic tanks) must be strictly isolated to the disposal zones of the West-North-West (WNW), preventing contamination of sacred and magnetic sectors. Furthermore, Varāhamihira's Dakārgala provides an empirically validated science of subterranean hydrology, bio-indicators, and natural coagulation.
tools.variation_note: Significant geographical and regional traditions govern water vāstu: 1. Kerala tradition (Manuṣyālaya Candrikā): In Kerala's high-rainfall maritime climate, digging the domestic well (Kūpa) in the Parjanya or Pūṣan pada is the mandatory first ritual preceding all construction; complex rainwater harvesting channels direct sloped-roof runoff into granite cisterns (Kulam), with strict avoidance of the Karṇa-sūtra (diagonal cords). 2. Western Indian / Rajasthani tradition (Viśvakarma Prakāśa, Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra): In arid climates, subterranean step-wells (Vāpī/Bāoli) and shaded courtyard water cisterns (Taṅkā) were engineered with thick sandstone walls to prevent evaporation. 3. Eastern / Bengal tradition: Village ponds (Pukur) were strategically excavated to the North-East or East of homesteads, serving dual roles as fish nurseries and morning solar reflectors.

tools.interpretation:
In classical Vedic architecture, the main doorway (Mahādvāra) is regarded as the literal mouth (Mukha) of the cosmic organism, the Vāstupuruṣa. Just as the mouth ingests physical nutrients and atmospheric prana for the physiological body, the Mahādvāra absorbs and modulates the solar, geomagnetic, and cosmic currents that animate the homestead.

From a scientific bio-energetic perspective:
1. East Entrances (Jayanta E3 & Indra E4): These positions welcome the benign, gentle infrared and therapeutic ultraviolet morning rays (06:00 to 08:30 hrs). These early rays stimulate human serotonin and vitamin D synthesis while sterilizing indoor atmospheres without thermal overheating. Conversely, E1 (Śikhi) lies too close to the sensitive North-East node where organic prana should enter unimpeded by human activity, while E7 and E8 border the fierce Agni node where excessive heat generates irritable psychological temperaments.

2. North Entrances (Mukhya N3, Bhallāṭa N4, Soma N5): The northern quadrant receives the continuous geomagnetic field lines flowing from the Earth's magnetic core (Jaiva-Urja). By placing the entrance in these central northern padas, the occupants' bio-magnetic field aligns constructively with the terrestrial flux, inducing deep parasympathetic calmness, mental concentration, and financial prudence. Hence, texts associate Bhallāṭa and Soma with Kubera's treasury.

3. West Entrances (Sugrīva W3, Puṣpadanta W4, Varuṇa W5): By afternoon, solar rays turn intensely hot and carry dehydrating infrared radiation. Sugrīva and Puṣpadanta face the cooling oceanic winds (governed by Varuna) that temper evening temperatures, making these portals magnificent for commercial enterprise, scholarly contemplation, and lineage longevity.

4. South Entrances (Gṛhakṣata S4 & Yama S5): While folk misconceptions label all south doors as unfavorable, classical treatises explicitly glorify S4 and S5. The South is ruled by Mars and Yama, representing structural integrity, legal order, and valor. Entrances here are ideal for institutions, administrators, and resilient families, provided the threshold is properly elevated to prevent geothermal thermal leakage.
tools.variation_note:
A notable distinction exists between the Northern Nagara traditions (Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra, Viśvakarma Prakāśa) and the Southern Dravidian traditions (Mayamata, Mānasāra, Manuṣyālaya Candrikā).

1. Grid Calibration: Northern texts calculate door padas primarily on the 81-pada Paramasāyika grid by dividing the exterior façade into 8 equal functional spans. Southern treatises frequently utilize the 64-pada Maṇḍūka grid for sacred buildings and royal dwellings, wherein the central doors occupy two full padas instead of one.

2. Evaluation of Yama and Varuṇa: In the Kerala tradition (Manuṣyālaya Candrikā), entrances in the South and West must pass an additional dimensional test called the Dvāra-Āyādi. Even if placed in Gṛhakṣata or Sugrīva, if the house Yoni does not harmonize with the facing direction, the door must be shifted or internally baffed.

tools.interpretation:
The orientation of a building represents its primary interface with the cosmic geometry of the Earth. Classical Indian treatises demonstrate extraordinary mathematical sophistication by requiring that house orientation be determined through the solar gnomon (Śaṅku-sthāpana) to ascertain the True Astronomical Meridian, rather than relying on the Earth's shifting magnetic field.

When a house is oriented within 0° to 5° of True North (Siddha-mukha), its walls coincide with the natural cardinal grid lines of geomagnetic force (Soma-sūtra running North-South) and solar movement (Brahma-sūtra running East-West). This alignment minimizes internal magnetic shear stress and optimizes human circadian biology:
1. East-facing structures capture the morning biological solar spectrum (stimulating neuroendocrine balance) while shielding the interior from excessive afternoon heat.
2. North-facing structures harvest benign, diffuse celestial light (reflected from the northern sky) and the soothing geomagnetic influx, promoting deep mental focus, stress reduction, and commercial clarity.
3. South and West facing structures require thicker masonry, smaller window openings, and deep roof overhangs to attenuate intense afternoon solar irradiance, but when harmonized with Yoni 3 (Siṃha) or Yoni 5 (Vṛṣabha), they foster tremendous material power and institutional durability.

The Āyādi Ṣaḍvarga formulas function as a sacred dimensional algorithm. By modulating the building's perimeter, the master architect ensures that the structure's physical acoustic-resonant footprint vibrates in constructive interference with the owner's natal birth star (Nakṣatra) and that financial gains (Āya) systematically outpace expenses (Vyaya).
tools.variation_note:
A deep regional divergence exists in how orientation canons are applied across India:

1. Kerala / Southern Tradition (Manuṣyālaya Candrikā): In Kerala Vastu, the Yoni of the house takes absolute precedence over all other considerations. A house facing East must strictly possess Yoni 1 (Dhvaja); a South-facing house must have Yoni 3 (Siṃha); a West-facing house must have Yoni 5 (Vṛṣabha); and a North-facing house must have Yoni 7 (Gaja). Even Yonis (2, 4, 6, 8) are considered an unpardonable architectural sin (Vāstu-doṣa). Furthermore, Kerala texts mandate rigorous local solar declination correction (Carā-saṃskāra) applied to the gnomon shadow.

2. Central and Western Tradition (Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra of King Bhoja): Malwa and Rajasthani traditions allow greater flexibility for civic dwellings facing the four cardinal directions, emphasizing perimeter Ayadi ratios and internal courtyard (Chatuḥśāla) ventilation to counter arid desert climates.

3. Modern Energy Vastu / Compass Calibration: In modern urban settings where plots are constrained by municipal road grids, magnetic compasses are standard. However, failure to account for local Magnetic Declination (which varies from -2° to +4° across India and up to ±15° globally) frequently causes consultants to misclassify an E3 door as E5, or a North facing house as North-North-East. This calculator's integrated magnetic declination algorithm resolves this classical flaw with geodetic precision.

tools.interpretation: Staircase Vastu (Sopāna-Vidhi) governs the vertical circulation cores that bridge floor diaphragms and transport energy vertically throughout a multi-storey structure. Mechanically, a staircase represents one of the most substantial dead loads in a building, concentrating severe shear forces and torsional loads at its base stringers. According to the foundational dictum 'Nairṛtye Guru, Īśāne Laghu' (Heavy in the South-West, Light in the North-East), staircases must anchor the terrestrial quadrants (SW, S, W) to counteract overturning moments and preserve the sacred lightness of the North-East and Brahmasthāna. Furthermore, human biomechanics during vertical climbing require that movement follow a clockwise (Pradakṣiṇā) direction, which works cooperatively with the Earth's geomagnetic rotational field. The number of steps must terminate on an odd number so that the ascent concludes with the auspicious right foot, and must yield a remainder of 1 (Indu) or 2 (Jaya) when divided by 3, avoiding the depleting zero remainder of Vyaya (loss).
tools.variation_note: Regional traditions reveal subtle structural adaptations: (1) In Kerala's timber architecture (Manuṣyālaya Candrikā), internal stairs were historically rare in single-storey homes and were built as steep wooden companion ladders (Sopāna-paṭṭikā) leading to attic granaries (Taṭṭu), often oriented externally along the veranda perimeter; (2) In North Indian stone and palace architecture (Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra), broad monumental masonry flights with intermediate resting landings (Sthagitaka) and carved balustrades (Hasti-hasta) were standard, mandating odd counts per individual flight; (3) Folk Vastu often asserts that 'any odd number of steps is acceptable', whereas classical Agamic texts insist on the rigorous modulo 3 filter (excluding 9, 15, and 21 as Vyaya-doṣa); (4) For modern multi-storey buildings with mid-landing turns, classical scholars treat each continuous flight between landings as a distinct energetic movement, while computing the floor-to-floor total for cumulative vibrational harmony.

tools.interpretation: Toilet and bathroom design in classical Vāstu Shastra represents one of the world's earliest systematic codes of preventive epidemiology, environmental sanitation, and bio-energetic zoning. Classical Sanskrit treatises make a fundamental ontological distinction between Snāna (sacred purification through clean, living water) and Śauca (the sanitary voiding of human metabolic waste). Pure water bathing belongs to the solar East and North-East, where early ultraviolet rays sterilize the damp atmosphere and stimulate human endocrine vitality. Conversely, human waste disposal (Utṣarga-sthāna) is strictly relegated to zones designed for detoxification and dispersal: West-North-West (WNW, ruled by Asura and Śoṣa, the deities of biological release and drying), South-South-West (SSW, the zone of metabolic excretion and expenditure), and North-West (Vāyavya, where the kinetic wind element rapidly dilutes and sweeps away foul ammoniacal gases and methane). Classical texts pronounce severe prohibitions against locating toilets in the North-East (Īśāna, the cosmic crown and spiritual receptor), the South-West (Nairṛtya, the earth foundation and marital anchor), and the Brahmasthāna (the cosmic navel and heart). Polluting these sensitive nodes with human excreta causes severe systemic pathologies: neurological disorders, financial ruin, relationship breakdown, and chronic morbidity. The mandatory alignment for the commode user—facing North or South—harmonizes the human colon with the Earth's geomagnetic meridians, assisting natural peristalsis while strictly honoring the sacred solar trajectory.
tools.variation_note: Traditional and regional architectural practices reveal fascinating evolutionary adaptations across India's geographical zones. In the traditional Kerala timber architecture documented in Manuṣyālaya Candrikā and Tantrasamuccaya, toilets were never permitted inside the main residential wooden dwelling (Nālukettu or Ettukettu). Instead, they were constructed as completely detached outdoor privies (Kākṣi-veśma) in the outer Vāyavya (North-West) compound, safely separated from the central Ayana and positioned downstream from the sacred domestic well (Kiṇaru) situated in the North-East. In the arid and rocky terrains of Western India and the Deccan palaces documented in Samarāṅgaṇa Sūtradhāra and Aparājitapṛcchā, elaborate gravity-assisted stone conduits (Praṇāla) and ventilated turrets were engineered on outer ramparts in the North-West, discharging waste into deep exterior subterranean soakways (Gartas) away from internal aquifers. In contemporary 21st-century multi-storey apartments where bathrooms are embedded inside bedrooms and plumbing stacks are structurally fixed by civil engineers, classical Vastu adapts through micro-zoning: sub-dividing the master bedroom suite into 16 micro-zones to place the commode in the micro-WNW or micro-NW, using non-invasive elemental boundary remedies (copper, brass, lead, or aluminium floor strips), maintaining pneumatic door closures, and physically decoupling wet bathing zones from dry water closets.

formula.operation: Add the constituent digits of C_grand repeatedly until a single digit 1-9 is obtained: R = 1 + ((C_grand - 1) mod 9). Unlike Pythagorean numerology, 11, 22, and 33 are fully reduced to 2, 4, and 6 for their root classification, while their compound identities remain recorded in step 4.

formula.title: Planetary Lordship & Archetype Assignment

sacred_nine_exclusion_rule.rule_name: Sacred Exclusion of Nine in Chaldean Alphabet
sacred_nine_exclusion_rule.statement: In the Chaldean numerology tradition, the number 9 is omitted from the letter-value table. No single letter in the alphabet is assigned the value 9.
sacred_nine_exclusion_rule.philosophical_rationale: Ancient Chaldean, Babylonian, and Hebrew sages regarded the number 9 as the supreme, cosmic, and unnameable vibration of the Divine Creator, the mystery of creation and destruction, and the ultimate sphere of cosmic completion. Because mortal language cannot encapsulate the unmanifest absolute, earthly letters only span vibrations 1 to 8. However, when letters of a name are summed, the total may legitimately produce 9 as a compound or reduced root number, embodying the fiery, martial, and transformative energy of Mars.
